take.en: Self-learning skill layer for Claude Code — distills real sessions into skills, merges duplicates, and prunes what stops getting used.

explanation.en: AutoHarness is a Claude Code plugin that treats the skill library as a living system. While you work, hooks capture tool-heavy episodes, a reflector proposes add/merge/patch/delete intents, and a promoter is the only writer that lands validated skills into .claude/skills. It only touches skills it authored, keeps a per-skill ledger of why each change happened, and opens every session with an index of its own library so recall does not depend on the host guessing.

why.en: Static skill packs rot the week after you install them. Founders running Claude Code all day need the harness to keep its own playbooks current from real work — not another dump of SKILL.md files and not a separate labeling job. AutoHarness is that missing lifecycle: learn, fold, graduate, archive.

howItWorks.en: In Claude Code run marketplace add tigerless-labs/autoharness, install autoharness@autoharness, then reload plugins. Zero config after that: tool-call cadence triggers background reflection, /learn forces a distill of the current session, and env knobs tune reflect/consolidate rates and capacity. State lives under .claude/autoharness/ and ~/.claude/autoharness/; skills land as normal native files the host already knows how to load.

different.en: Skill packs and one-shot recorders freeze a lesson once. AutoHarness keeps running beside the host: merge same-scenario skills instead of stacking twins, prune by usage rate after probation, and never rewrite hand-written skills. Same model, different harness — the bet is the skill layer can maintain itself.
